title: TypeScript SDK: runtime discriminant inference and Zod guard helpers for streaming shape recovery
creator: Jonah Kim
description:
Problem: TypeScript SDK users need a robust, ergonomic way to recover strongly-typed shapes from streaming model outputs and partial tokens. Existing discriminated-union patterns break when a discriminator token arrives late or when streaming introduces partial JSON fragments.

Goal: Ship a runtime discriminant inference layer plus Zod guard helpers that: (1) infer the most likely discriminant from partial/streaming output, (2) provide best-effort runtime guards (Zod) and TypeScript-friendly type narrowing helpers, and (3) integrate with the SDK's streaming utilities so callers can validate incremental chunks and receive typed events when a concrete shape is resolved.

Why this matters: Many upstream customers rely on structured outputs for business logic (invoices, order items, API-like responses). Streaming is used to reduce latency and cost; losing strong typing during streaming increases production errors and pushes validation responsibility back to customers. This work should reduce integration friction, lower errors, and enable safe progressive rendering and early fallback strategies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming responses can be incrementally validated: SDK emits transient 'partial' events and final 'validated' events when a Zod guard succeeds.
- Discriminant inference recovers correct union variant for >= 95% of real workload samples in internal eval set (see reference dataset).
- TypeScript helper types and generated type guards are exported under a clear API (zodGuardsFromSchema / inferDiscriminantFromStream).
- Backwards compatibility: existing non-streaming consumers keep current behavior unchanged.
- Tests: unit + integration covering partial fragments, late discriminator arrival, and adversarial token truncation.
- Documentation: README, examples (simple chat bot, invoice extraction streaming example), and migration notes for existing codegen users.
design_notes:
- We will add a small state machine per-stream that tracks: buffer, last-parsed-JSON, observed keys, and potential discriminants with confidence scores.
- Use Zod schemas (or JSON Schema) emitted by the model's contract metadata to seed candidate discriminants. If no schema exists, fall back to heuristic inference based on key presence and token-level regex heuristics.
- Expose two APIs: a high-level streaming validator that emits typed events (PartialFragment, TentativeMatch, Validated) and a low-level infer API that given a text fragment returns candidate discriminants with confidence scores.
- Avoid heavy runtime: keep infer heuristics O(n) on fragment size; cache compiled Zod guards for model+version combos.
- Provide an opt-in "strictMode" that delays emitting 'validated' until complete JSON parse and Zod parse succeed; default mode will allow best-effort validated events flagged as 'heuristic=true' to support optimistic UX flows.
implementation_plan:
1) Schema plumbing: extend model metadata surface to include JSON-schema/Zod-shape references or an S3 pointer for schema bundles.
2) Typeguard generator: adapt existing typegen pipeline to emit Zod runtime guards + lightweight TypeScript narrowers (codegen run for each model release).
3) Streaming state machine: implement in runtime streaming layer, write thorough unit tests for transitions and buffer handling.
4) Heuristics engine: implement candidate inference rules (key presence, primitive-type patterns, value shape hints).
5) Integration: wire SDK to emit events and provide example helpers.
6) End-to-end tests: run against corpus of 1200 representative streaming transcripts (internal eval set).
7) Docs + example PRs.
8) Canary: release behind feature flag 'streaming-type-guards' and run on dedicated test orgs for 2 weeks before enabling wider.
tradeoffs:
- Performance vs correctness: strictMode increases latency and token buffering; default heuristic mode favors UX but can produce false-positives.
- Complexity: adding runtime inference increases code surface and potential for subtle bugs in corner cases (truncated tokens, nested unions). Mitigation: opt-in and cache heavy paths.
- Bundle size: emitting Zod guards for many models could blow up client bundle. Mitigation: ship guards as separate packages or lazy-load via dynamic import and allow server-side validation in cloud-hosted flows.
- Coverage: heuristics may require continuous tuning on real customer data; will add telemetry to collect mismatch cases for future improvements.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for: buffer append/trim, candidate generation, confidence scoring, Zod guard caching.
- Integration tests (local): simulated streaming responses where discriminator arrives early/mid/late/never.
- E2E: run against 1200-sample internal dataset and assert >=95% correct discriminant resolution in default heuristics on non-adversarial set; run adversarial suite expecting documented failure modes.
- Fuzz tests: random truncate/inject to ensure graceful degradation and no runtime exceptions.
- CI: add gate that prevents merging without tests and a sample min-coverage metric for the new module.
- Monitoring: runtime metric 'streaming_type_guard.mismatch' and sample logging (scrubbed) for failed inference cases.
rollout:
- Feature flag: streaming-type-guards default OFF.
- Stage 1: internal dogfood in SDK-team org for 3 days.
- Stage 2: enable for 2 non-critical customer orgs (opt-in) and monitor mismatch and latency (2 weeks).
- Stage 3: enable as opt-out for all SDK customers with telemetry and a quick revert if mismatch spikes.
- Communication: release notes, migration guide and opt-in example PRs in examples/streaming-guards.
- Post-release followups: collect mismatch samples and schedule tuning sprint if mismatch > 5% on non-adversarial workload.
